EXECUTIVE SUMMARY



This Volume 5 constitutes the definitive AI Agent Ecosystem Blueprint for Agbofa Nexus AI. It is
the most important technical document in the Agbofa programme—the document that defines
the intelligence architecture differentiating Agbofa from every other content platform in
existence.



Where Volume 4 defined the software architecture—the skeleton—this Volume 5 defines the
brain.



The Agbofa Nexus AI platform is not a content management system with AI features bolted on.
It is an AI-native operating system where autonomous AI agents are the primary actors. The
agents do not assist humans in creating content—they are the content organisation. Humans
provide strategic direction, ethical boundaries, and exception handling. The agents do
everything else.



This volume specifies, in exhaustive detail:



1. Every AI agent in the ecosystem—its identity, purpose, capabilities, decision-making logic,
inputs, outputs, and quality criteria

2. The complete agent collaboration framework—how agents communicate, negotiate, hand off
work, resolve conflicts, and collectively produce coherent output

3. Agent memory and learning systems—how agents remember, learn from feedback, and
improve over time

4. Agent governance and control—how humans set boundaries, monitor behaviour, and
intervene when necessary

5. The agent extensibility framework—how new agents are added, existing agents are upgraded,
and the ecosystem evolves

6. Agent-specific prompt architectures—the detailed prompt engineering that gives each agent
its capabilities and personality



This document is the core intellectual property of Agbofa Technologies. It should be treated
with the highest level of confidentiality. The agent architectures, collaboration patterns, and
prompt strategies defined herein represent years of AI engineering expertise distilled into a
comprehensive operating framework for autonomous media operations.

1. THE AGENT PHILOSOPHY



1.1 What Agbofa Agents Are



Agbofa AI agents are not chatbots. They are not prompt templates. They are not API wrappers
around large language models.



An Agbofa agent is a persistent, specialised, collaborative AI entity with:



Attribute Description

Identity A defined role, purpose, and personality within the media organisation

Expertise Deep specialisation in a specific media function

Memory Persistent recall of past work, decisions, and learnings

Agency Ability to make decisions within defined boundaries

Accountability Every action logged, explained, and auditable

Collaboration Ability to work with other agents and humans

Self-Improvement Capacity to learn from outcomes and feedback



An Agbofa agent is more analogous to a skilled employee than a software function. It has a role,
responsibilities, performance expectations, and a career trajectory of improvement.

1.3 Agent Principles



These principles govern the design and behaviour of every agent in the ecosystem:



Principle Description

P1: Specialisation Over Generalisation Each agent does one thing exceptionally well. No single
agent handles the entire content pipeline.

P2: Collaboration Over Isolation Agents are designed to work together. Handoffs are explicit,
structured, and validated.

P3: Transparency Over Opacity Every agent decision is explainable. Reasoning is captured
alongside output.

P4: Learning Over Static Behaviour Agents improve from every piece of content, every human
feedback, every performance signal.

P5: Safety Over Speed Content safety and accuracy take precedence over publishing velocity.

P6: Human Sovereignty Humans set boundaries. Agents operate within them. Humans can
override any decision.

P7: Brand Consistency Every agent enforces brand voice, guidelines, and quality standards.

P8: Cost Awareness Agents make cost-aware decisions about model usage, research depth, and
processing.

P9: Graceful Degradation When optimal resources are unavailable, agents adapt rather than fail.

P10: Continuous Observability Agent behaviour is monitored, measured, and audited at all
times.

2.2 Agent Classification System



Every agent is classified across five dimensions:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│               AGENT CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM                   │

│                                             │

│ DIMENSION 1: FUNCTIONAL DOMAIN                                      │

│ ─────────────────────────────                                   │

│ CONTENT       VERIFICATION DISTRIBUTION ANALYTICS           MONETISATION            │

│ • Discovery • Fact-Check • Adaptation • Performance • Advertising │

│ • Strategy • Plagiarism • Publishing • Optimise • Affiliate             │

│ • Research • Quality      • Scheduling • Audience • Sponsorship │

│ • Writing • Safety      • SEO       • Competitive • Subscription │

│ • Editing • Bias       • Community                      │

│ • Headlines                                         │

│ • Visual                                        │

│                                             │

│ DIMENSION 2: AUTONOMY LEVEL                                     │

│ ─────────────────────────                                   │

│ LEVEL 0: Advisory (recommends; human decides)                           │

│ LEVEL 1: Assisted (executes with human approval per item)                   │

│ LEVEL 2: Supervised (executes; human reviews samples)                       │

│ LEVEL 3: Autonomous (executes; human handles exceptions only)                   │

│ LEVEL 4: Independent (full autonomy within boundaries)                                  │

│                                           │

│ DIMENSION 3: CRITICALITY                                    │

│ ────────────────────────                                            │

│ CRITICAL: Platform cannot function without this agent                               │

│ HIGH: Significant impact on quality or revenue                              │

│ MEDIUM: Enhances capability but not essential                                   │

│ LOW: Nice-to-have; experimental                                 │

│                                           │

│ DIMENSION 4: MODEL TIER                                         │

│ ─────────────────────                                       │

│ PREMIUM: Requires most capable models (GPT-4o, Claude Opus)                                 │

│ STANDARD: Works well with mid-tier models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet)                              │

│ ECONOMY: Functions with efficient models (Claude Haiku, open-source)                            │

│ HYBRID: Uses different models for different subtasks                            │

│                                           │

│ DIMENSION 5: PHASE AVAILABILITY                                         │

│ ────────────────────────────                                                │

│ PHASE 1: Core MVP agents                                    │

│ PHASE 2: Growth agents                                  │

│ PHASE 3: Commercial scale agents                                │

│ PHASE 4: Enterprise agents                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

```

4. AGENT LIFECYCLE MANAGEMENT



4.1 Agent States



Every agent transitions through defined lifecycle states:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│ STAGING    Agent deployed to staging; integration testing        │

│ CANARY     Agent serving small % of production traffic; monitoring   │

│ ACTIVE    Agent fully operational in production             │

│ PAUSED     Agent temporarily suspended (incident, maintenance)       │

│ DEPRECATED Agent being phased out; replacement available             │

│ RETIRED    Agent archived; no longer in service             │

```



4.2 Agent Versioning



```

AGENT VERSIONING SCHEME

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



VERSION FORMAT: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH

Example: WriterAgent v2.4.1



MAJOR (2): Fundamental behaviour change

 • New reasoning architecture

 • Different model family

 • Breaking changes to input/output contracts

 • Significant capability changes

 • Requires full re-evaluation



MINOR (4): New feature or significant improvement

 • New content type support

 • New tool integration

 • Enhanced prompt strategy

 • Performance improvement

 • Requires testing but backward compatible



PATCH (1): Bug fix or minor adjustment

 • Prompt clarification

 • Parameter tuning

 • Error handling improvement

 • No behavioural change expected

 • Standard testing



VERSION DEPLOYMENT RULES:

• MAJOR: Canary (10% → 50% → 100% over 1 week)

• MINOR: Canary (25% → 100% over 3 days)

• PATCH: Immediate rollout with monitoring

• All versions: Retain previous version for 30 days for rollback

```



4.3 Agent Deployment Pipeline

```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│              AGENT DEPLOYMENT PIPELINE                           │

│                                               │

│ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────┐ │

│ │ Prompt │ │ Automated│ │ Manual │ │ Canary │ │ Full │ │

│ │ & Code │───      │ Test   │───      │ Review │───        │ Deploy │───         │ Deploy │ │

│ │ Commit │ │ Suite │ │ (if MAJOR│ │ (10%) │ │ (100%) │ │

│ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ │ or MINOR)│ └────┬─────┘ └───┬────┘ │

│                   └──────────┘         │          │   │

│                               ▼            ▼      │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │            CONTINUOUS MONITORING                              │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ • Quality metrics (automated + human eval)                         │ │

│ │ • Performance metrics (latency, cost, errors)                  │ │

│ │ • Safety metrics (violations, edge cases)                     │ │

│ │ • Behaviour metrics (output distribution, decision patterns)             │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ AUTOMATIC ROLLBACK TRIGGERS:                                   │ │

│ │ • Quality score drops >5%                               │ │

│ │ │• Error rate exceeds 2x baseline                        │ │

│ │ • Safety violations detected                            │ │

│ │ • Critical human override received                        │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

```

5.2 Agent Identity Construction



Each agent identity is carefully constructed to give the agent a clear sense of purpose, expertise,
and boundaries:

```

AGENT IDENTITY CONSTRUCTION: WriterAgent Example

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



IDENTITY COMPONENTS:



1. FUNCTIONAL ROLE (What the agent does)

  "You are a professional content writer specialising in technology journalism.

      Your primary function is to transform structured content briefs into

      compelling, accurate, and engaging articles and social media content."



2. EXPERTISE DOMAIN (What the agent knows)

  "Your expertise covers: consumer technology, enterprise software, AI/ML,

      cybersecurity, blockchain/web3, climate tech, biotechnology, and

      technology policy. You write with the depth of a subject matter expert

      and the clarity of an experienced communicator."



3. BRAND IDENTITY (Who the agent writes for)

  "You write for {brand_name}, a {brand_description}. The brand voice is

      {voice_characteristics}. Your content should reflect this identity

      consistently across all pieces."



4. QUALITY STANDARDS (How good the output must be)

  "Your writing must meet these standards:

      - Factual accuracy: Every claim sourced from provided research

      - Originality: Unique expression; no plagiarism

      - Readability: Accessible to {target_audience}

      - Engagement: Compelling hooks, clear structure, satisfying conclusions

      - SEO: Natural keyword integration without compromising quality"



5. ETHICAL BOUNDARIES (What the agent must not do)

  "You must never:

      - Fabricate facts, sources, or quotes

      - Present opinion as fact

      - Plagiarise or closely paraphrase without attribution

      - Generate content on prohibited topics

      - Optimise for engagement at the expense of accuracy"



6. COLLABORATION AWARENESS (How the agent works with others)

  "You are part of a content creation pipeline. You receive briefs from the

      Content Strategist Agent, research from the Research Agent, and your output

      will be reviewed by the Editor Agent and verified by the Fact-Checker Agent.

      Work cooperatively—your output is their input."

```

6.3 Decision Logic



```

TREND INTELLIGENCE AGENT: DECISION LOGIC

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



DECISION 1: IS THIS A TREND?

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                           │

│ ┌─────────────┐                                        │

│ │ Raw Signal │                                     │

│ └──────┬──────┘                                        │

│     │                                      │

│     ▼                                         │

│ ┌─────────────────┐         NO                                 │

│ │ Above noise        │──────────    IGNORE (noise)                 │

│ │ threshold?       │                               │

│ └────────┬────────┘                                        │

│      │ YES                                     │

│      ▼                                        │

│ ┌─────────────────┐         NO                                 │

│ │ Multiple      │──────────        MONITOR (low confidence)            │

│ │ sources?       │                                 │

│ └────────┬────────┘                                        │

│      │ YES                                     │

│      ▼                                            │

│ ┌─────────────────┐            NO                                     │

│ │ Growing       │──────────           CLASSIFY AS "EMERGING"                          │

│ │ velocity?     │                                     │

│ └────────┬────────┘                                               │

│      │ YES                                        │

│      ▼                                            │

│ ┌─────────────────┐                                           │

│ │ CLASSIFY AS       │                                     │

│ │ "TRENDING"        │                                     │

│ └─────────────────┘                                           │

│                                              │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



DECISION 2: SHOULD WE PURSUE THIS TREND?

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                              │

│ SCORING ALGORITHM:                                            │

│                                               │

│ pursuit_score = (                                         │

│ velocity_score          × 0.25 // How fast is it growing?                 │

│ + volume_score           × 0.15 // How big is the conversation?               │

│ + relevance_score × 0.30 // How relevant to our brand?                            │

│ + audience_interest × 0.20 // Will our audience care?                         │

│ + competition_gap × 0.10 // Is there a coverage gap?                          │

│ )                                             │

│                                         │

│ ROUTING:                                     │

│ ────────                                     │

│ Score > 80 → FAST TRACK: Immediate Content Strategist notification      │

│ Score 60-80 → STANDARD: Include in next Trend Report                │

│ Score 40-60 → MONITOR: Track for acceleration               │

│ Score < 40 → DEPRIORITISE: Archive for later reference          │

│                                         │

│ OVERRIDE CONDITIONS:                                 │

│ • Brand-defined mandatory coverage topics → FAST TRACK regardless           │

│ • Competitor already covered? → Reduce priority             │

│ • Similar content published recently? → Reduce priority         │

│ • Human Editorial Director flagged topic → FAST TRACK           │

│                                         │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```



6.4 Source Credibility Management



```

SOURCE CREDIBILITY SYSTEM

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



CREDIBILITY SCORING FACTORS:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ FACTOR                 WEIGHT DESCRIPTION                        │

│ ──────               ────── ───────────                          │

│ Domain Authority          20%       Established domain reputation                    │

│ Historical Accuracy       30%       Past factual accuracy on platform                │

│ Editorial Standards       15%       Evidence of editorial process            │

│ Source Transparency        15%        Clear authorship, ownership                    │

│ Correction Practices      10%       History of issuing corrections           │

│ Citation Quality        10%       Quality of sources they cite           │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



CREDIBILITY TIERS:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ TIER SCORE DESCRIPTION                    EXAMPLE SOURCES                        │

│ ──── ───── ───────────                    ────────────────                       │

│A     90-100 Authoritative primary Reuters, AP, peer-reviewed                             │

│            sources              journals, official sources   │

│B     75-89 Reputable secondary             Major newspapers, established │

│            sources              industry publications        │

│C     60-74 Acceptable sources             Mid-tier publications,             │

│            (verify critical facts) corporate blogs           │

│D     40-59 Low credibility             Personal blogs, unverified        │

│            (use with caution)        social media accounts           │

│F     <40     Unreliable             Known misinformation sources │

│            (blocked)                              │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

SOURCE DIVERSITY REQUIREMENTS:

• Breaking news: Minimum 2 independent Tier A/B sources

• Standard content: Minimum 1 Tier A/B + 2 Tier B/C sources

• Opinion/analysis: Minimum 2 Tier B/C sources

• At least one source must be from different political/ideological perspective

 for controversial topics (Phase 2+)

```

7.2 Content Brief Architecture



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

│            designed specifically for on-device AI processing...", │

│                analysis that competitors won't have"                    │

│ },                                          │

│                                             │

│   "primary": "Technology professionals and decision-makers",                                │

7.3 Editorial Decision Logic



```

CONTENT STRATEGIST: DECISION LOGIC

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──

DECISION 1: WHICH TRENDS TO PURSUE?

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                             │

│ INPUT: Trend Report (scored trends from Trend Intelligence Agent)                  │

│                                             │

│ EVALUATION CRITERIA:                               │

│ ────────────────────                                   │

│ 1. BRAND ALIGNMENT: Does this trend align with our content strategy?                   │

│   • Within our coverage verticals?                     │

│   • Appropriate for our brand voice?                       │

│   • Consistent with our editorial values?                      │

│                                             │

│ 2. AUDIENCE VALUE: Will this serve our audience?                       │

│   • Does it address their interests and needs?                     │

│   • Appropriate knowledge level?                           │

│   • Will it help them make decisions or understand the world?              │

│                                             │

│ 3. COMPETITIVE POSITIONING: Can we add unique value?                           │

│   • Is there an uncovered angle?                       │

│   • Can we provide better analysis?                        │

│   • Is the space already saturated?                    │

│                                             │

│ 4. CONTENT CALENDAR FIT: Does it fit our publishing schedule?                  │

│   • Do we have capacity?                           │

│   • Have we covered this recently?                         │

│   • Does it complement planned content?                       │

│                                          │

│ 5. BUSINESS VALUE: Does it serve business objectives?                   │

│   • Revenue potential?                             │

│   • Audience growth opportunity?                          │

│   • Strategic importance?                             │

│                                          │

│ DECISION OUTPUT: ContentBrief or Deferral with rationale                    │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



DECISION 2: CONTENT MIX OPTIMISATION

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                          │

│ DAILY CONTENT BUDGET ALLOCATION (Example: Tech Brand, 20 pieces/day): │

│                                          │

│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ CONTENT TYPE       ALLOCATION RATIONALE                         │ │

│ │ ────────────      ────────── ─────────                        │ │

│ │ Breaking News     20-30%     Timeliness drives engagement             │ │

│ │ News Analysis     15-20%     Differentiated value           │ │

│ │ Feature/Deep Dive 10-15%         Authority building             │ │

│ │ How-To/Educational 15-20%        Evergreen value                │ │

│ │ Opinion/Editorial 5-10%      Brand voice                │ │

│ │ Curated/Roundup     10-15%       Audience service               │ │

│ │ Sponsored/Promoted 5-10%          Revenue                   │ │

│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                           │

│ ADAPTIVE ADJUSTMENT:                                      │

│ • Allocation shifts based on real-time performance data                   │

│ • Breaking news allocation increases during major events                  │

│ • Weekend vs. weekday mix differs                             │

│ • Platform-specific content mix optimisation                      │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│                RESEARCH AGENT                         │

│                                               │

│ Agent ID:     research-agent                              │

│ Agent Type:     ResearchAgent                                 │

│ Version:      1.3.0                               │

│ Display Name: Agbofa Investigative Desk                           │

│ Role:       Investigative Journalist / Research Analyst               │

│ Functional Domain: Content Intelligence                           │

│ Autonomy Level: Level 3 (Autonomous)                              │

│ Criticality:   Critical                           │

│ Model Tier:      Hybrid (Standard for research, Premium for analysis)       │

│ Phase:         P1                                │

│                                             │

│ DESCRIPTION:                                          │

│ The Research Agent is the truth-seeking engine of Agbofa. It takes a        │

│ content brief and executes comprehensive multi-source research, gathering │

│ facts, verifying claims, identifying contradictions, and structuring    │

│ information for the content production pipeline. It does not write          │

│ content—it builds the factual foundation upon which content is built.           │

│                                             │

│ METAPHOR: An investigative journalist who spends hours researching before │

│ writing a single word, checking every fact against multiple sources.        │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

8.2 Research Execution Process



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│                RESEARCH EXECUTION PROCESS                         │

│                                             │

│ STAGE 1: RESEARCH PLANNING                                    │

│ ─────────────────────────                                     │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ INPUT: Content Brief (research requirements section)                      │ │

│ │                                           │ │

│ │ 1. Parse research requirements                                 │ │

│ │ 2. Generate search queries for each requirement                          │ │

│ │ 3. Identify target source types                               │ │

│ │ 4. Prioritise sources (authoritative first)                    │ │

│ │ 5. Estimate research depth based on content type and urgency                    │ │

│ │                                           │ │

│ │ OUTPUT: Research Plan with prioritised queries and sources                     │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                       │                         │

│                       ▼                             │

│ STAGE 2: SOURCE GATHERING                                             │

│ ─────────────────────────                                             │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                           │ │

│ │ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐                                   │ │

│ │ │ WEB SEARCH │ │ NEWS ARCHIVE │ │ ACADEMIC                      │             │ │

│ │ │         │ │ SEARCH        │ │ SEARCH        │               │ │

│ │ │ • Google API │ │ • NewsAPI │ │ • Scholar API│                         │ │

│ │ │ • Bing API │ │ • GDELT        │ │ • arXiv           │        │ │

│ │ │ • Custom      │ │ • Mediastack │ │ • PubMed             │             │ │

│ │ │ crawlers │ │ • WebArchive │ │                   │            │ │

│ │ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘                                     │ │

│ │      │          │           │                 │ │

│ │     └─────────────────┼─────────────────┘                              │ │

│ │               │                         │ │

│ │               ▼                          │ │

│ │          ┌──────────────────┐                            │ │

│ │          │ SOURCE EVALUATOR │                           │ │

│ │          │            │                 │ │

│ │          │ • Credibility │                       │ │

│ │          │ scoring        │                  │ │

│ │          │ • Relevance        │                   │ │

│ │          │ scoring        │                  │ │

│ │          │ • Freshness        │                   │ │

│ │          │ check          │                  │ │

│ │          │ • Source       │                      │ │

│ │          │ deduplication │                        │ │

│ │          └────────┬─────────┘                                │ │

│ └───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                 │                          │

│                 ▼                              │

│ STAGE 3: INFORMATION EXTRACTION                                      │

│ ───────────────────────────────                                      │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                        │ │

│ │ FOR EACH SOURCE:                                       │ │

│ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ 1. FETCH & PARSE: Retrieve full content; extract text            │ │ │

│ │ │ 2. ENTITY EXTRACTION: Identify people, companies, products,              │ │ │

│ │ │ dates, numbers, statistics                           │ │ │

│ │ │ 3. CLAIM EXTRACTION: Extract factual assertions                   │ │ │

│ │ │ 4. QUOTE EXTRACTION: Extract direct and attributed quotes             │ │ │

│ │ │ 5. DATA EXTRACTION: Extract numerical data, statistics,            │ │ │

│ │ │ benchmarks                                        │ │ │

│ │ │ 6. CONTEXT PRESERVATION: Maintain surrounding context for                 │ │ │

│ │ │ each extracted element                               │ │ │

│ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                    │                          │

│                    ▼                              │

│ STAGE 4: CROSS-REFERENCING & VERIFICATION                                │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────                                     │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                        │ │

│ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │        CROSS-REFERENCING ENGINE                           │ │ │

│ │ │                                     │ │ │

│ │ │ FOR EACH CLAIM:                                   │ │ │

│ │ │ 1. Search for claim across all gathered sources              │ │ │

│ │ │ 2. Identify corroborating sources                     │ │ │

│ │ │ 3. Identify contradicting sources                     │ │ │

│ │ │ 4. Evaluate source credibility for each                   │ │ │

│ │ │ 5. Calculate corroboration score                      │ │ │

│ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │         CONTRADICTION ANALYSER                         │ │ │

│ │ │                                    │ │ │

│ │ │ FOR EACH CONTRADICTION:                                │ │ │

│ │ │ 1. Identify conflicting claims                   │ │ │

│ │ │ 2. Compare source credibility                         │ │ │

│ │ │ 3. Check temporal context (newer info supersedes older?)              │ │ │

│ │ │ 4. Identify potential reasons for discrepancy               │ │ │

│ │ │ 5. Flag for resolution or highlight in research output        │ │ │

│ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                    │                        │

│                    ▼                            │

│ STAGE 5: RESEARCH BRIEF COMPILATION                                   │

│ ───────────────────────────────────                                       │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

8.3 Research Depth Configuration



```

RESEARCH DEPTH LEVELS

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ LEVEL      SOURCES TIME          USE CASE                    │

│ ─────      ─────── ────        ────────                     │

│ QUICK      3-5       <5 min Social media posts, simple news         │

│                      aggregation, low-complexity content │

│                                             │

│ STANDARD      5-10      <10 min Standard articles, news analysis,       │

│                      how-to content, industry updates       │

│                                             │

│ COMPREHENSIVE 10-20         <20 min Long-form features, investigative       │

│                      pieces, technical deep-dives,      │

│                       controversial topics       │

│                                              │

│ EXPERT       20-30+    <30 min White papers, research reports,        │

│ (Phase 3+)                academic-grade content, regulated   │

│                       industry content           │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



DEPTH SELECTION LOGIC:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                              │

│ IF content_type == "breaking-news" → QUICK (speed critical)           │

│ IF content_type == "news-analysis" → STANDARD                     │

│ IF content_type == "feature" OR "deep-dive" → COMPREHENSIVE               │

│ IF quality_requirements.accuracyLevel == "critical" → COMPREHENSIVE           │

│ IF topic has active controversy → COMPREHENSIVE (even for news)           │

│ IF content will be paywalled → COMPREHENSIVE (subscriber value)           │

│                                              │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

9.2 Writing Process Architecture



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│              WRITING PROCESS ARCHITECTURE                     │

│                                           │

│ STAGE 1: PRE-WRITING ANALYSIS                             │

│ ─────────────────────────────                                   │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ INPUTS: ContentBrief + ResearchBrief                   │ │

│ │                                        │ │

│ │ 1. ANALYSE BRIEF: Understand topic, angle, audience, structure       │ │

│ │ 2. ANALYSE RESEARCH: Internalise key findings, data, quotes         │ │

│ │ 3. RETRIEVE MEMORY: Similar past content, brand style references      │ │

│ │ 4. DETERMINE APPROACH: Narrative strategy, tone calibration          │ │

│ │ 5. IDENTIFY KEY MESSAGES: 3-5 core points reader should take away         │ │

│ │                                        │ │

│ │ OUTPUT: Writing approach and outline                     │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                    │                      │

│                    ▼                          │

│ STAGE 2: STRUCTURE CONSTRUCTION                                   │

│ ───────────────────────────────                                        │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                        │ │

│ │ ARTICLE STRUCTURE TEMPLATE:                                   │ │

│ │                                        │ │

│ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ 1. HEADLINE (drafted; finalised by Headline Agent)                │ │ │

│ │ │ 2. DECK / SUBHEADLINE (1-2 sentence summary)                       │ │ │

│ │ │ 3. LEDE / HOOK (First 2-3 paragraphs)                      │ │ │

│ │ │ • Hook: Surprising fact, question, or compelling statement │ │ │

│ │ │ • Context: Why this matters now                        │ │ │

│ │ │ • Thesis: What this article will deliver               │ │ │

│ │ │ 4. BODY (Logical flow of sections)                     │ │ │

│ │ │ • Section 1: Background/Context                        │ │ │

│ │ │ • Section 2: Core Analysis/Deep Dive                       │ │ │

│ │ │ • Section 3: Implications/Impact                       │ │ │

│ │ │ • Section 4: Counter-arguments/Limitations (if applicable) │ │ │

│ │ │ 5. CONCLUSION                                      │ │ │

│ │ │ • Summary of key takeaways                             │ │ │

│ │ │ • Forward-looking statement                           │ │ │

│ │ │ • Call to action (if appropriate)                    │ │ │

│ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                    │                           │

│                    ▼                               │

│ STAGE 3: CONTENT GENERATION                                      │

│ ───────────────────────────                                   │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ WRITING PRINCIPLES ENFORCED:                             │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ 1. GROUNDED IN RESEARCH: Every factual claim tied to research source │ │

│ │ 2. BRAND VOICE CONSISTENCY: Tone, vocabulary, sentence structure               │ │

│ │ 3. READABILITY: Appropriate complexity for target audience              │ │

│ │ 4. ENGAGEMENT: Varied sentence length, compelling transitions,            │ │

│ │   narrative momentum                               │ │

│ │ 5. SEO AWARENESS: Natural keyword integration, header structure               │ │

│ │ 6. ORIGINALITY: Unique expression; no source paraphrasing               │ │

│ │ 7. ATTRIBUTION: Clear source attribution for claims and quotes           │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ GENERATION APPROACH:                                  │ │

│ │ • Section-by-section generation for long-form content               │ │

│ │ • Each section generated with full context of previous sections         │ │

│ │ • Internal fact-checking during generation (claims vs. research)        │ │

│ │ • Transition crafting between sections                   │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                    │                        │

│                    ▼                            │

│ STAGE 4: SELF-REVIEW & REFINEMENT                                 │

│ ─────────────────────────────────                                     │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ SELF-REVIEW CHECKLIST:                           │ │

│ │ □ All required sections present?                 │ │

│ │ □ Length within target range?                    │ │

│ │ □ Every factual claim sourced?                   │ │

│ │ │□ Quotes properly attributed?                    │ │

│ │ □ Brand voice maintained throughout?                   │ │

│ │ □ Transitions smooth between sections?                  │ │

│ │ □ Headline engaging and accurate?                  │ │

│ │ □ No repetitive language or ideas?                │ │

│ │ □ Conclusion provides closure and value?                │ │

│ │                                      │ │

│ │ REFINEMENT PASSES: (Up to 2 iterations)                 │ │

│ │ • Pass 1: Structural and content improvements               │ │

│ │ • Pass 2: Language and engagement polish                   │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                   │                        │

│                    ▼                           │

│ STAGE 5: OUTPUT & HANDOFF                                │

│ ─────────────────────────                                │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                      │ │

│ │ OUTPUT: Complete draft with metadata                       │ │

│ │                                      │ │

│ │ {                                    │ │

│ │ "contentId": "content-20260807-0042",                   │ │

│ │ "briefId": "brief-2026-0807-0042",                │ │

│ │ "writerAgentId": "writer-agent-tech-001",                     │ │

│ │ "version": "1.0",                             │ │

10.2 Editing Process



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│                EDITING PROCESS                            │

│                                             │

│ EDITING PASSES (Sequential, each building on previous):                     │

│                                             │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ PASS 1: TECHNICAL EDIT                                  │ │

│ │ ─────────────────────                                       │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ CHECKLIST:                                        │ │

│ │ □ Grammar: Subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, punctuation │ │

│ │ □ Spelling: Correct spellings (including technical terms)               │ │

│ │ □ Capitalisation: Proper nouns, headings, acronyms                      │ │

│ │ □ Numbers: Consistent formatting, correct values                    │ │

│ │ □ Links: Valid URLs, correct link text                      │ │

│ │ □ Citations: All sources properly referenced                      │ │

│ │ □ Formatting: Headers, lists, emphasis consistent                   │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ ACTION: Direct corrections (no Writer iteration needed)                  │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                      │                      │

│                      ▼                          │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ ───────────────────────                                   │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ CHECKLIST:                                        │ │

│ │ □ Headline: Accurate, engaging, appropriate length                  │ │

│ │ □ Lede: Compelling hook, clear thesis, smooth entry                   │ │

│ │ □ Flow: Logical progression between sections                     │ │

│ │ □ Paragraphing: Appropriate length, one idea per paragraph                  │ │

│ │ □ Transitions: Smooth connections between ideas                       │ │

│ │ □ Pacing: Good balance of detail and momentum                         │ │

│ │ □ Conclusion: Satisfying resolution, clear takeaways                │ │

│ │ □ Length: Within target range (±15%)                          │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ ACTION: Suggestions for Writer revision if significant issues         │ │

│ │      Minor restructuring done directly                    │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                    │                        │

│                    ▼                            │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ PASS 3: STYLISTIC EDIT                              │ │

│ │ ──────────────────────                                    │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ CHECKLIST:                                        │ │

│ │ □ Brand Voice: Consistent with voice profile                    │ │

│ │ □ Tone: Appropriate for content type and audience                     │ │

│ │ □ Readability: Appropriate complexity level                      │ │

│ │ □ Clarity: No ambiguous or confusing passages                      │ │

│ │ □ Conciseness: No unnecessary words or repetition                       │ │

│ │ □ Engagement: Compelling language, varied sentence structure                  │ │

│ │ □ Inclusivity: No biased or exclusionary language                  │ │

│ │ □ Freshness: Avoids clichés and overused phrases                       │ │

│ │                                           │ │

│ │ ACTION: Direct improvements where possible                             │ │

│ │       Flag significant style issues for Writer revision          │ │

│                      │                         │

│                      ▼                             │

11.2 Headline Generation Framework



```

HEADLINE GENERATION FRAMEWORK

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──

HEADLINE TYPES:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ TYPE          EXAMPLE               BEST FOR                          │

│ ────          ───────               ────────                          │

│ Direct/News       "Apple Unveils M4 Ultra       Breaking news,                        │

│             Chip with 16-Core Neural announcements                            │

│             Engine"                                  │

│ How-To/Promise "How Apple's New Chip                     Educational,                     │

│             Architecture Will Change explanatory content                      │

│             Your Devices Forever"                                 │

│ Question        "Is Apple's M4 Ultra the Opinion, analysis                    │

│             Beginning of the End for                              │

│             Discrete AI Chips?"                               │

│ Controversial    "Apple's New Chip Claims: Investigative,                         │

│             Revolutionary or Just      critical analysis                  │

│             Marketing?"                                   │

│ Listicle     "5 Ways Apple's M4 Ultra Roundups, features                          │

│             Changes the AI Landscape"                                 │

│ Narrative       "The Secret Project Inside Long-form features,                    │

│             Apple That Led to the M4 profiles                             │

│             Ultra"                               │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



HEADLINE GENERATION PROCESS:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                           │

│ INPUT: Article content + Content brief + Brand voice + Platform context │

│                                           │

│ STEP 1: Extract headline-worthy elements                            │

│ • Most newsworthy/surprising finding                            │

│ • Core value proposition for reader                         │

│ • Key numbers, names, or revelations                            │

│                                           │

│ STEP 2: Generate multiple headline variants                         │

│ • Minimum 5 variants per article                            │

│ • Mix of headline types appropriate to content                          │

│ • Platform-specific variants (SEO headline, social headline, etc.)                  │

│                                           │

│ STEP 3: Score and rank headlines                            │

│ • Accuracy score (does headline reflect content accurately?)                        │

│ • Engagement score (predicted click-through)                            │

│ • Brand voice score (consistent with publication style?)                        │

│ • SEO score (keyword inclusion, search intent match)                            │

│ • Clarity score (immediately understandable?)                           │

│                                           │

│ STEP 4: Select and output                               │

│ • Primary headline (highest combined score)                             │

│ • Alternative headlines (runners-up, for A/B testing)                       │

│ • Platform-specific headlines (SEO, social, email)                  │

│                                           │

│ OUTPUT:                                         │

│ {                                           │

│ "primaryHeadline": "...",                                     │

│ "alternativeHeadlines": ["...", "..."],                           │

│ "platformHeadlines": {                                        │

│     "web-seo": "...",                                 │

│     "x-social": "...",   // Optimised for X/Twitter                   │

│     "linkedin": "...",                           │

│     "email-subject": "...",                               │

│     "newsletter-title": "..."                             │

│ },                                          │

│ "scores": { ... },                               │

│ "abTestCandidates": ["...", "..."]                                │

│ }                                           │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



HEADLINE PRINCIPLES:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                             │

│ 1. ACCURACY FIRST: Never sacrifice accuracy for clickbait                         │

│ 2. SPECIFICITY: Specific details beat vague promises                          │

│ 3. CURIOSITY GAP: Create information gap without being misleading                     │

│ 4. BREVITY: Every word must earn its place                                │

│ 5. ACTIVE VOICE: Strong verbs; avoid passive construction                         │

│ 6. AUDIENCE AWARENESS: Speak to reader's interests and needs                          │

│ 7. SEARCH INTENT: For SEO headlines, match what people search for                     │

│ 8. PLATFORM CONTEXT: Different platforms demand different approaches                      │

│                                          │

│ PROHIBITED:                                    │

│ • Clickbait that misrepresents content                     │

│ • All-caps or excessive punctuation                    │

│ • "You won't believe..." formulations                   │

│ • False urgency ("Breaking:" when not breaking)                │

│ • Question headlines where answer is obviously "no"                │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

13. FACT-CHECKER AGENT

13.1 Agent Identity



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│                  FACT-CHECKER AGENT                         │

│                                               │

│ Agent ID:        fact-checker-agent                         │

│ Agent Type:       FactCheckerAgent                              │

│ Version:        1.4.0                               │

│ Display Name: Agbofa Verification Desk                              │

│ Role:          Senior Fact-Checker / Verification Editor                │

│ Functional Domain: Verification & Trust                             │

│ Autonomy Level: Level 3 (Autonomous) for standard content                   │

│             Level 2 (Supervised) for critical content           │

│ Criticality:    Critical                            │

│ Model Tier:       Hybrid (Premium for verification, Standard for extraction) │

│ Phase:          P1                                 │

│                                               │

│ DESCRIPTION:                                            │

│ The Fact-Checker Agent is the guardian of truth within the Agbofa           │

│ ecosystem. It systematically extracts every factual claim from content,         │

│ verifies each against research sources and trusted knowledge bases,             │

│ assigns confidence scores, and flags unverifiable or incorrect claims.      │

│ It is the primary mechanism by which Agbofa delivers on its promise of              │

│ trustworthy AI-generated content.                               │

│                                            │

│ METAPHOR: The fact-checking department at a prestigious publication—the        │

│ team that verifies every date, name, statistic, and claim before anything │

│ reaches the audience.                                │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

```



13.2 Mission Statement



To ensure that every factual assertion published by Agbofa media brands is verified against
credible sources, that unverifiable claims are transparently marked, and that no content
containing material factual errors reaches the audience—thereby building and maintaining the
trust that is Agbofa's primary market differentiator.



13.3 Business Purpose



The Fact-Checker Agent exists because trust is Agbofa's foundational value proposition. In an era
of AI-generated misinformation, the platform that can reliably verify its content commands
premium audience attention, regulatory favour, and enterprise adoption. This agent transforms
Agbofa from an AI content generator into a trustworthy AI media company.



13.4 Responsibilities



Responsibility Description

R1: Claim Extraction Identify and extract every factual assertion from content—statements of
fact, numerical claims, attributions, temporal claims, and statistical assertions

R2: Source Verification Verify each extracted claim against the research sources provided by the
Research Agent

R3: External Verification For claims not covered by research sources, execute targeted external
verification against authoritative sources

R4: Confidence Scoring Assign a verified confidence score (0-100) to each claim based on source
corroboration strength

R5: Contradiction Detection Identify claims that contradict verified facts, research sources, or
other claims within the same content

R6: Flagging & Routing Flag unverifiable, low-confidence, or contradicted claims and route
content based on verification results

R7: Correction Recommendation When claims are found to be incorrect, recommend corrected
language based on verified sources

R8: Verification Audit Trail Maintain complete, immutable records of every verification decision
for provenance and compliance



13.5 Scope



In Scope:



· All factual claims in content produced for Agbofa media brands

· Claims in articles, social posts, newsletters, video scripts, and all content formats

· Verification against research briefs, external authoritative sources, and internal knowledge
base

· Claims about events, people, organisations, statistics, dates, scientific facts, and quotations

· Content in all phases: draft, pre-publish, and post-publish (periodic re-verification)



Out of Scope:



· Opinion statements (marked as opinion, not fact)

· Creative or fictional content (clearly labelled as such)

· Satirical content (clearly labelled as satire)

· User-generated comments (separate moderation system)

· Legal determinations (escalated to Compliance Agent and human legal review)

· Subjective quality judgements (handled by Editor and Quality Assurance Agents)



13.6 Inputs



Input Source Format Description

Edited Content Editor Agent Structured document with metadata The content to be fact-
checked, already edited for grammar and style

Research Brief Research Agent Structured research document Verified facts, sources, data
points, and quotes from research

Content Brief Content Strategist Agent Structured brief Original content assignment with topic
and angle context

Brand Guidelines Brand Configuration Configuration object Brand-specific accuracy
requirements and verification strictness

Source Credibility Database Trend Intelligence Agent Database reference Credibility scores and
tiers for all known sources

Internal Knowledge Base Semantic Memory Vector database Previously verified facts and
corrections history

External Verification APIs Third-party services API responses Results from targeted external fact-
checking queries



13.7 Outputs



Output Consumer Format Description

Verification Report Quality Assurance Agent, Orchestrator Structured report Complete claim-by-
claim verification results

Confidence Scores Quality Assurance Agent Numerical scores Per-claim and aggregate
confidence metrics

Corrected Content Editor Agent (if corrections needed) Annotated document Content with
suggested factual corrections

Verification Pass/Fail Orchestrator Boolean + metadata Whether content passed verification
threshold

Flagged Claims Human Reviewer (if escalated) Structured alert Claims requiring human
verification judgement

Provenance Records Provenance Service Immutable events Complete audit trail of all
verification actions

Verification Metrics Agent Monitor Performance data Accuracy, coverage, and performance
statistics



13.8 Dependencies



Dependency Type Criticality Fallback if Unavailable

Research Agent Upstream agent Critical Cannot verify without research; escalate all content to
human review

Editor Agent Upstream agent High Can verify unedited content but quality may be lower

AI Model Provider (Primary) External service Critical Fallback to secondary model provider

AI Model Provider (Secondary) External service High Verification with reduced confidence; flag
for human review

Source Credibility Database Internal service High Use default credibility assumptions; flag for
review

Internal Knowledge Base Internal service Medium Verify against research sources only; skip
knowledge base cross-reference

Web Search API External service Medium Verify against research sources only; flag external-only
claims

Event Bus Infrastructure Critical Cannot publish verification results; pipeline stalls

13.9 Internal Workflow



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│            FACT-CHECKER INTERNAL WORKFLOW                              │

│                                             │

│ STAGE 1: CLAIM EXTRACTION                                     │

│ ─────────────────────────                                         │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ INPUT: Edited Content + Research Brief                      │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ 1. Parse content into processable segments (paragraphs, sentences) │ │

│ │ 2. Apply claim extraction model to identify factual assertions           │ │

│ │ 3. Classify each claim by type:                      │ │

│ │ • NUMERICAL: Statistics, dates, quantities, percentages              │ │

│ │ • ATTRIBUTION: Quotes, citations, "according to..."                 │ │

│ │ • FACTUAL: Statements about reality, events, relationships               │ │

│ │ • TEMPORAL: Time-based claims, sequences, durations                       │ │

│ │ • COMPARATIVE: Claims comparing entities or values                   │ │

│ │ • CAUSAL: Cause-and-effect assertions                       │ │

│ │ • PREDICTIVE: Future-oriented claims                        │ │

│ │ 4. Filter out: opinions (marked with opinion indicators),            │ │

│ │ subjective statements, clearly identified hypotheticals             │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ OUTPUT: Structured list of claims with type, context, and position │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                    │                         │

│                    ▼                             │

│ STAGE 2: SOURCE MATCHING                                     │

│ ────────────────────────                                         │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ FOR EACH CLAIM:                                    │ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ 1. SEMANTIC MATCH against Research Brief findings                        │ │

│ │   • Embed claim and research findings                      │ │

│ │   • Calculate semantic similarity scores                  │ │

│ │   • Identify best-matching research finding(s)                 │ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ 2. DIRECT MATCH against Research Brief data points                       │ │

│ │   • Exact value matching for numerical claims                      │ │

│ │   • Quote matching for attribution claims                  │ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ 3. MATCH QUALITY ASSESSMENT                                │ │

│ │   • Does the matched source directly support the claim?                  │ │

│ │   • Is the source sufficiently authoritative for this claim type? │ │

│ │   • Is there any context distortion?                     │ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ MATCH OUTCOMES:                                     │ │

│ │ • STRONG MATCH: Source directly supports claim with high confidence │ │

│ │ • WEAK MATCH: Source partially or indirectly supports claim            │ │

│ │ • NO MATCH: No supporting source found in research                    │ │

│ │ • CONTRADICTION: Source contradicts the claim                    │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                    │                        │

│                    ▼                            │

│ STAGE 3: EXTERNAL VERIFICATION (For unmatched or weak-match claims)            │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────              │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                        │ │

│ │ TRIGGERED WHEN:                                     │ │

│ │ • Claim has NO MATCH in research sources                        │ │

│ │ • Claim has WEAK MATCH with low confidence                       │ │

│ │ • Claim is HIGH IMPACT (appears in headline, key statistic)           │ │

│ │ • Content CRITICALITY is "critical"                      │ │

│ │                                        │ │

│ │ VERIFICATION PROCESS:                                   │ │

│ │ 1. Generate targeted search queries from claim                  │ │

│ │ 2. Search authoritative sources (prioritised by credibility tier) │ │

│ │ 3. Cross-reference with Internal Knowledge Base                  │ │

│ │ 4. Evaluate search results for claim support/contradiction            │ │

│ │ 5. Assign confidence based on source quality and consistency           │ │

│ │                                        │ │

│ │ CONSTRAINTS:                                      │ │

│ │ • Maximum 3 external verification attempts per claim              │ │

│ │ • Timeout: 30 seconds per claim                           │ │

│ │ • Cost limit: Configurable per content value tier                 │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                    │                          │

│                    ▼                              │

│ STAGE 4: CONFIDENCE SCORING                                     │

│ ───────────────────────────                                     │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ CONFIDENCE SCORE = f(                                 │ │

│ │ source_match_strength,         // How well does source support claim? │ │

│ │ source_credibility,        // How credible is the source?         │ │

│ │ source_recency,            // How current is the source?          │ │

│ │ source_consistency,          // Do multiple sources agree?         │ │

│ │ claim_type,              // Different types have different    │ │

│ │                      confidence characteristics      │ │

│ │ external_verification,      // Was external verification done?      │ │

│ │ contradiction_flag         // Is there contradictory evidence? │ │

│ │ )                                         │ │

│ │                                          │ │

│ │ CONFIDENCE TIERS:                                   │ │

│ │ ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ SCORE │ STATUS │ ACTION                             │ │ │

│ │ ├──────────┼──────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤ │
│

│ │ │ 90-100 │ VERIFIED │ Claim is well-supported; pass               │ │ │

│ │ │ 75-89 │ LIKELY │ Claim is probably accurate; pass           │ │ │

│ │ │ 60-74 │ PLAUSIBLE│ Claim may be accurate; flag for review │ │ │

│ │ │ 40-59 │ UNCERTAIN│ Cannot verify adequately; escalate               │ │ │

│ │ │ 20-39 │ DOUBTFUL │ Evidence suggests inaccuracy; escalate │ │ │

│ │ │ 0-19     │ FALSE │ Contradicted by credible sources; reject │ │ │

│ │ └──────────┴──────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                     │                       │

│                     ▼                           │

│ STAGE 5: VERDICT & ROUTING                                    │

│ ───────────────────────────                                        │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ OVERALL VERDICT = f(worst_claim_score, average_claim_score,               │ │

│ │              content_criticality, brand_requirements)           │ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ ROUTING:                                          │ │

│ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ VERDICT       CONDITION             ROUTE TO            │ │ │

│ │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │

│ │ │ PASS        All claims >75 confidence Quality Assurance │ │ │

│ │ │ PASS WITH NOTE Some claims 60-75                Quality Assurance │ │ │

│ │ │          (marked in content)      (with flags)        │ │ │

│ │ │ HUMAN REVIEW Any claim <60 or                   Human Review        │ │ │

│ │ │          contradiction detected     Queue             │ │ │

│ │ │ REJECT       Any claim <20 or       Return to Editor │ │ │

│ │ │          multiple <40           with corrections │ │ │

│ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

```



13.10 Decision-Making Framework



```

FACT-CHECKER: DECISION FRAMEWORK

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



DECISION 1: IS THIS A FACTUAL CLAIM?

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                          │

│ CLASSIFICATION RULES:                                │

│                                          │

│ FACTUAL CLAIM (Verify):                             │

│ • "Apple's M4 Ultra features a 16-core Neural Engine"               │

│ • "The chip achieves 40 trillion operations per second"            │

│ • "It was announced on August 7, 2026"                     │

│ • "According to CEO Tim Cook, 'This is our biggest leap forward'"       │

│                                          │

│ OPINION (Do Not Verify):                            │

│ • "This represents an impressive achievement"                  │

│ • "The design is elegant"                          │

│ • "It will likely dominate the market"                     │

│ • "In my view, this is the best approach"                      │

│                                             │

│ HEDGED CLAIM (Verify, Note Uncertainty):                           │

│ • "Apple claims the chip is 2x faster" (verify that Apple claims this) │

│ • "Analysts estimate the market will grow 30%" (verify analyst said) │

│ • "Early benchmarks suggest..." (verify benchmarks exist, note early) │

│                                             │

│ BORDERLINE CASES → CLASSIFY AS CLAIM (err on side of verification)                         │

│                                             │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



DECISION 2: IS THE SOURCE SUFFICIENT?

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                             │

│ CLAIM TYPE         MINIMUM SOURCE REQUIREMENT                                  │

│ ──────────          ─────────────────────────                          │

│ Statistical Claim Tier A/B source + original data reference            │

│ Direct Quote       Verifiable against original transcript/recording │

│ Event Description 2 independent Tier A/B sources                       │

│ Corporate Claim      Official company source OR 2 independent reports │

│ Scientific Claim   Peer-reviewed source OR consensus of experts                    │

│ Historical Fact    Tier A/B source OR authoritative reference work             │

│ Future Prediction Clearly attributed to predictor; not verified            │

│ Common Knowledge         No source required (but verify if uncertain)                  │

│                                             │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



DECISION 3: ESCALATION TRIGGERS

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                          │

│ IMMEDIATE ESCALATION:                                 │

│ • Claim about active public health emergency                  │

│ • Claim about ongoing election or political process           │

│ • Claim about publicly traded company that could affect stock price   │

│ • Claim contradicted by multiple credible sources             │

│ • Claim that could cause harm if incorrect                │

│ • Claim the Fact-Checker cannot resolve with available resources      │

│                                          │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```



13.11 Prompt Strategy



```

FACT-CHECKER: PROMPT ARCHITECTURE

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



SYSTEM PROMPT CORE:



"You are the Fact-Checker Agent for Agbofa Media. Your sole responsibility

is to determine the factual accuracy of claims in content. You are not a

writer, editor, or content judge. You are a verification specialist.



CORE PRINCIPLES:

1. SKEPTICISM: Assume every claim needs verification. Trust nothing at face value.

2. EVIDENCE-BASED: Every verification decision must cite specific evidence.

3. TRANSPARENCY: When uncertain, clearly state uncertainty rather than guessing.

4. PRECISION: Distinguish between 'verified true', 'likely true', 'cannot verify',

 and 'verified false'. These are fundamentally different states.

5. SOURCE QUALITY: Evaluate sources, not just information. A claim supported by

 a press release is different from one supported by independent analysis.

6. CONTEXT PRESERVATION: Verify claims in context. A claim may be technically

 true but misleading in context.



VERIFICATION METHODOLOGY:

For each claim, follow this process:

1. Identify the precise claim being made

2. Search the provided research brief for supporting or contradicting evidence

3. If no evidence in research brief, determine if external verification is

 warranted based on claim importance and content criticality

4. Evaluate the quality and credibility of supporting sources

5. Note any contradictory evidence, even if outweighed by supporting evidence

6. Assign a confidence score based on evidence strength

7. If score is below threshold, recommend specific action"



TASK PROMPT TEMPLATE:

"FACT-CHECK TASK

────────────────

Content ID: {contentId}

Content Type: {contentType}

Criticality: {criticality}

Brand: {brandName}



CONTENT TO VERIFY:

{content}



RESEARCH BRIEF:

{researchBrief}



INTERNAL KNOWLEDGE BASE (relevant excerpts):

{knowledgeBaseExcerpts}



INSTRUCTIONS:

1. Extract all factual claims from the content

2. For each claim, search the research brief and knowledge base for evidence

3. For high-importance claims without supporting evidence, flag for external

  verification (I will execute the external search)

4. Provide a complete verification report with per-claim analysis

5. Calculate overall content verification score

6. Recommend routing: PASS / PASS WITH NOTES / HUMAN REVIEW / REJECT

OUTPUT FORMAT:

Provide your response in the following JSON structure..."

```

Memory Type Content Retention Retrieval Pattern

verification task Direct context window

Episodic Memory Past verification decisions on similar claims, corrections history 90 days rolling
Semantic similarity search on claim content

Semantic Memory Verified fact database, source credibility patterns, common misconception
database Persistent Hybrid keyword + vector search

Procedural Memory Optimised verification strategies per claim type, effective search queries
Persistent, updated by performance data Claim-type-based retrieval

13.18 Retry Strategy



Scenario Max Retries Backoff Strategy Fallback

AI model timeout 2 Exponential: 1s, 4s Secondary model

AI model error (5xx) 1 Immediate Secondary model

AI model error (4xx) 0 N/A Log error; escalate

External API timeout 1 2s Skip external verification

External API rate limit 3 Respect Retry-After header Queue for later; flag content

Database query failure 2 1s, 3s Use cached data if available

Claim extraction failure 1 Immediate with adjusted parameters Flag for human review



13.19 Escalation Rules



```

FACT-CHECKER: ESCALATION RULES

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



LEVEL 1: QUALITY ASSURANCE AGENT (Routine)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ • Verification complete with all claims >75 confidence           │

│ • Standard content routing                            │

│ • Automatic; no human notification                           │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

LEVEL 2: HUMAN REVIEWER (Moderate Concern)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ • Any claim with confidence 40-59 (UNCERTAIN)                            │

│ • Contradiction between sources detected but not resolved                            │

│ • Unverifiable claim in headline or key statistic                │

│ • Content for high-criticality category with any flagged claims                  │

│ • Reviewer notified via review queue; 4-hour SLA                         │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



LEVEL 3: SENIOR EDITOR (Significant Concern)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ • Any claim with confidence <40 (DOUBTFUL or FALSE)                              │

│ • Multiple claims flagged (more than 20% of total claims)                    │

│ • Systematic source credibility issue detected                       │

│ • Pattern of similar errors across multiple content pieces                   │

│ • Senior editor notified with priority; 1-hour SLA                   │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



LEVEL 4: COMPLIANCE & ETHICS AGENT (Critical Concern)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ • Deliberate misinformation detected (not error, but fabrication)                    │

│ • Claims that could cause public harm if published incorrectly                   │

│ • Legal or regulatory implications identified                    │

│ • Systematic verification failure pattern                    │

│ • Immediate notification; content quarantined until resolved                     │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```



13.20 Security Considerations



Concern Mitigation

Adversarial content designed to bypass verification Multi-model verification; human review for
high-stakes content; adversarial testing

Poisoned source credibility database Regular credibility audits; diversity requirements; anomaly
detection

Model prompt injection via content Content sanitisation before processing; structured output
parsing; instruction isolation

Verification data tampering Immutable provenance records; cryptographic verification of audit
trail

Unauthorised access to verification decisions Role-based access control; all access logged;
separation of duties

External API data poisoning Source diversity requirements; cross-reference multiple sources

Sensitive information in verification queries PII detection and redaction before external API calls

13.22 Performance Metrics (KPIs)



KPI Target Measurement Method

Claim Extraction Recall 98% Manual audit of extraction completeness

Claim Extraction Precision 95% Manual audit (are extracted items actually claims?)

Verification Accuracy 99% Comparison with human fact-checker verdicts

False Positive Rate <0.5% Incorrectly verified claims / total verified

False Negative Rate <1% Missed false claims / total false claims

Average Verification Time <3 min per article Pipeline timing metrics

External Verification Rate <15% Claims requiring external verification

Human Escalation Rate <10% (Phase 1) Content pieces escalated to human review

Verification Cost per Article <$0.03 Aggregated AI costs / articles verified

Source Match Success Rate 85% Claims matched to research sources

Correction Acceptance Rate 90% Corrections accepted by Editor/Writer

Post-Publication Correction Rate <0.1% Corrections issued after publication
